Q007.t: A retriever returns every neutral ball. Which thought keeps patience active rather than passive?

Q009.t: In a tiebreak against a pusher, you notice yourself shortening rallies that worked throughout the set. What is the best reset?

Q013.t: A huge server stays back after serving and you can only block the return. What is the safest neutralising target?

Q015.t: A body serve crowds your forehand hip. Which response creates usable contact fastest?

Q017.t: Facing a dominant first serve, which goal creates the most useful pressure over a return game?

Q020.t: Your return contact is late on first serves but comfortable on second serves. Which adjustment is most intelligent?

Q025.t: Two waist-high balls land inside the baseline. On the first you are balanced; on the second you are reaching. Which is smart aggression?

Q029.t: After missing an easy forehand at 5–4, 15–all, what belongs in the next 20 seconds?

Q038.t: At 5–5 in a tiebreak, which serve plan best controls pressure?

Q042.t: In a tiebreak, which shot best represents smart aggression from a neutral ball?

Q044.t: You lead 6–4 in a tiebreak and have the next serve. Which plan best uses the advantage?

Q047.t: After an error, which use of body language is most valuable?

Q049.t: Why can “one point at a time” improve decisions late in a match?

Q053.t: Your partner’s serve stretches the returner wide and their shoulders open early toward crosscourt. What is the best poach read?

Q054.t: Both doubles opponents are balanced near the baseline. Why can a firm middle ball be valuable?

wide_serve.g: Move the returner wide, read the actual reply, then use the space.

serve_plus_one.g: Test the familiar return, confirm it, then play behind the recovery.

down_the_line.g: Build the rally until a shorter ball and balance earn the change.

short_ball.g: Use the transition ball, then let the next contact decide the finish.

net_approach.g: Follow a suitable approach and read the first volley you actually receive.

drop_lob.t: Bring Them Forward, Read the Reply
drop_lob.g: Change the deep defender’s court. Keep reading after they reach the short ball.

high_ball_backhand.g: Read depth first: step in only when time and balance support the contact.

pass_or_lob.g: Make the first volley difficult, then use the space the closing player leaves.
